summary: P2 (the deterministic inter-switch bound the paper rests on) carried no single-cycle non-crossing condition, and the paper's own admissible boundary instance (E_0=0.03, D_max=0.95, dt=0.05) lets an alternating maximal advantage flip the class every cycle while satisfying P2; repaired post-adjudication in 3eaf1a0 on aris/hardening-v0.8 (not re-reviewed)
audited_at_commit: d8c21e2 (branch aris/hardening-v0.8; the round-3 repair commit, unchanged for 17 days before this round)

protocol_notes: headline_unstable rule deliberately overridden for the third time: the abstract changed in d8c21e2 and the round exists to test whether the round-3 repairs closed the P1 attack surface

round-3 attack axis (P1 drift/Kingman) did not reappear; the zero-context attacker moved to P2 vacuity and to the liveness/evaluation gap, an indirect signal the round-3 repairs shifted the attack surface

attack arithmetic (E_0/(D_max-Dfloor)=0.0333 s < dt=0.05 s; single-cycle innovation 0.045 > E_0 on the boundary instance) independently verified by the authors by recomputation before the adjudication returned; the N_min/non-vacuity repair route was pre-derived in the same verification

author-side finding raised by neither attacker nor adjudicator: the by-construction advantage bound is D_max = sum_X w_X = 2.8 for the default weights (each normalized term is clipped to [0,1] and summed with weights 1.0/1.0/0.3/0.5, cost_evaluator.cpp:119), not 1; the worst-case default N_min is therefore 3 cycles (0.15 s), reported in the paper as such rather than the 7 cycles that a single-term bound would give

author-side consistency defect fixed in passing: Algorithm 1 wrote J(c) as a horizon integral of already-normalized terms, inconsistent with Section 4.2 and the implementation (the integrals live inside J_X before normalization)

the adjudicator's 'then test the alternating-maximal-advantage sequence' was not executed in the harness (that would be a new measurement); the one-cycle flip on the boundary instance is exhibited analytically in rem:p2nonvac and the N_min bound is proved, not measured

all numbers added to the paper in this round (N_min 3/7/14, N_resp 76/24/17/7, reachability thresholds 0.23/0.41, equilibrium 0.583 vs 0.60, ramp end e~0.21) are consequences of the printed recursion and knob values, computed by script and labelled as derivations, not measurements

decomposed_points.post_audit_action: P2 restated as the discrete-cycle bound N_min(rho)=ceil(E_th(rho)/((D_max-Dfloor)dt)) with the declared non-vacuity condition E_0 > (D_max-Dfloor)dt (eq:p2nonvac, N_min>=2); abstract, contribution, scope paragraph and conclusion restated with the cycle bound and the condition

decomposed_points.label: admissible one-cycle counterexample (boundary instance)
decomposed_points.post_audit_action: eq:p2nonvac declared alongside eq:twosided; rem:p2nonvac shows the boundary instance violates it (0.045 > 0.03), exhibits the every-cycle flip, and excludes the instance as an operating point; rem:lockboundary annotated; default-knob N_min reported including the worst case D_max=2.8 (3 cycles) and D_max<=1 (7 cycles)

decomposed_points.label: P2 vacuity versus liveness (never switching satisfies P2)
decomposed_points.post_audit_action: new Proposition prop:p2live: under a sustained advantage D_k>=D_sus, a discretionary switch fires within N_resp=ceil(ln(1-E(1-lambda)/a)/ln lambda) cycles, with full monotone-comparison proof and a converse (no switch reachable when the leak equilibrium lies below the threshold); rem:resptime gives default-knob figures; P2 text now states it is a rate upper bound only

decomposed_points.post_audit_action: mechanism made exact via the converse clause (clean_commit advantage 0.40 gives equilibrium 0.583 < E_th(1)=0.60, so no switch is reachable once rho saturates); the recommended estimator change (rho from realized cross-track displacement) is an implementation change outside this text-only round and remains open; demonstration across the speed range requires measurement

decomposed_points.label: decision-stream metrics reward freezing
decomposed_points.post_audit_action: warranted-switch recall, response delay (vs N_resp) and lockup rate pre-registered for both the harness and the physical evaluation (Section 5.6); the decision-stream-only limitation is unchanged and closes only with the planned physical evaluation

details.net_assessment: The paper would probably not survive a senior area-chair reading of this attack. It candidly discloses the liveness, proxy, reversal, and freezing limitations, but those disclosures do not repair the headline mathematics: P2's own formally admissible witness allows cycle-rate discretionary switching, so the advertised deterministic anti-oscillation interpretation is unsupported.
top_action_items: Replace P2 with an exact discrete-cycle bound plus an explicit, nontrivial multi-cycle requirement (done in 3eaf1a0, pending round-5 re-review)
Add a complementary finite-response liveness theorem and repair the forward-speed-based progress estimator (theorem added in 3eaf1a0; estimator repair is an implementation change and remains open)
Evaluate warranted-switch correctness, response delay, freezing, and realized motion, not switch suppression alone (metrics pre-registered in 3eaf1a0; measurement not performed)
